idea-plugin.name: HDL and Vivado + MCP Support
idea-plugin.description:
Let an AI assistant drive Vivado — and keep the IDE it drives it from.

FPGA work means living in two windows: your editor for the RTL, and Vivado for everything else. This plugin closes that gap, and then goes further — it can hand your live Vivado session to an AI assistant, so building a block design or chasing a timing failure becomes a conversation instead of an afternoon of clicking.

AI assistants can drive your Vivado session

Connect Claude Code, Junie, Codex, or any client that speaks the Model Context Protocol, and it gets 27 curated, parameter-checked Vivado commands — the same ones you have. It can create and open projects, add sources, set the top module, build and wire block designs, apply board presets, run connection automation, assign addresses, generate HDL wrappers, run synthesis and implementation, produce a bitstream, and program a device.

Ask for what you want and watch it happen in the Vivado GUI:

  • "Create a Zynq project for my KV260, add the PS, and wire up an AXI GPIO."
  • "Synthesis failed — read the log and tell me what broke."
  • "Add these RTL files, set top to design_1_wrapper, and build a bitstream."

You stay in charge the whole time:

  • You start it, every time. The server never starts on its own, and a safety agreement explains what you are enabling before it opens.
  • Arbitrary Tcl is opt-in. The unrestricted-Tcl tools are hidden from the assistant and refused unless you enable them for that one session.
  • Locked down. Loopback only, no CORS headers, browser origins and rebound host names refused, and a fresh bearer token minted for every session.
  • Nothing happens silently. Every command is printed to the Vivado Console before it executes, so you watch the work as it happens — and you can type into the same session while the assistant works.
  • Vivado must be running. No live session means every tool is refused.

Vivado Console — the terminal underneath it

The same channel the assistant uses is yours to type into: a bidirectional Tcl terminal attached to a live Vivado session. Because it talks over a socket rather than stdin, the Vivado GUI stays fully usable while you work. 27 parameterised commands are available from a toolbar palette, with command history on the up/down arrows.

Language support

  • Verilog and SystemVerilog (.v .vh .sv .svh) — syntax highlighting, context-aware completion, commenting, and brace matching that pairs module/endmodule, begin/end, case/endcase and the rest.
  • Tcl and XDC (.tcl .xdc) — highlighting, code folding for proc bodies and braced blocks, ${var} handling, and completion for common Vivado commands.

Linting that understands your whole design

  • Real-time errors and warnings from Icarus Verilog or Verilator, inline in the editor.
  • Mark a folder as the Top Folder and the linter analyses your modules together — cross-file instantiations resolve instead of showing up as phantom errors.
  • A debugger panel with the raw tool output when you need to see exactly what ran.

Vivado and Vitis

  • Build a project from a folder of HDL, or open an existing .xpr.
  • Run a Tcl or XDC script from the project view (Ctrl+Alt+R).
  • Package IP through IP Composer, and open Vitis workspaces or create Vitis HLS kernels.

Requirements

  • IntelliJ IDEA 2025.1 or newer.
  • Xilinx Vivado (2023.2 or newer recommended) for the Vivado features — set the path in Settings → Tools → HDL Settings.
  • Icarus Verilog or Verilator for linting. Everything else works without them.

Source, issue tracker and documentation on GitHub.

Parts of this plugin were developed with AI assistance. Every release is reviewed and covered by an automated test suite; please report anything that looks wrong.
